stories.kicker: EXTRAORDINARY AUTUMN WARMTH · CENTRAL ASIA TO SIBERIA
stories.headline: A giant Eurasian heat dome drives temperatures up to 19 °C above late-November norms

beats.title: Spring-Like Air Where Deep Winter Should Stand
beats.text: Across southeastern Kazakhstan, afternoon temperatures have climbed to 14.0 °C at a time of year when the steppe normally sits near freezing. Further north across central Siberia, air that is typically locked near -25 °C has surged almost 20 °C above seasonal averages.

beats.title: Locked in Place for Four Straight Weeks
beats.text: This is no brief warm front. Daily tracking over the past month shows all 28 of the last 28 days in southeastern Kazakhstan and 24 of 28 days in northern Siberia running far warmer than normal beneath a stubborn, continent-spanning high-pressure ridge.

beats.title: Record-Setting in 87 Years of ERA5 Data
beats.text: Comparing today's warmth against every late-November record since 1940 in the Copernicus ERA5 archive, the Kazakh steppe anomaly ranks #1 in 87 years (99.4th percentile), while the northern Siberian surge stands 4th warmest on record (96th percentile).

beats.title: Arctic Amplification Reshaping Autumn
beats.text: Northern Siberia has warmed by +2.4 °C in late November since 1940-1979, doubling the frequency of top-decile warm extremes between the mid-20th century and the post-1986 era as retreating snow and sea ice amplify continental heating.

stories.kicker: RELENTLESS FLOODING RAIN · ADRIATIC & WESTERN BALKANS
stories.headline: Another 137 mm deluge batters the Adriatic coast after two weeks of soaking storms

beats.title: Warm Mediterranean Moisture Slams Coastal Mountains
beats.text: Southerly gales gusting to 25 m/s are driving a rich plume of Mediterranean moisture straight into the steep Dinaric Alps, squeezing out 137 mm of fresh rain in 24 hours along the coasts of Montenegro and southern Croatia.

beats.title: Nearly 700 mm in a Single Fortnight
beats.text: This storm arrives on ground that cannot absorb another drop: 10 of the past 14 days have brought heavy rain here, piling up an astonishing 676 mm over two weeks as successive Mediterranean depressions stall against Balkan high ground.

beats.title: Top 4% of Late-November Rainstorms Since 1940
beats.text: Across 87 years of ERA5 records back to 1940, today's regional rainfall intensity ranks 4th highest for late November (96th percentile), following a string of destructive autumn lows across southern Europe.

beats.title: A Warmer Mediterranean Fuels Heavier Downpours
beats.text: Late-November air temperatures along the Adriatic have risen +1.4 °C since 1940-1979, allowing the atmosphere to hold roughly 10% more water vapour; 90th-percentile autumn rain days here have tripled from 2 to 6 per 40-year era.

stories.headline: Fierce 973 hPa North Pacific cyclone lashes Kamchatka with 147 km/h gusts

beats.title: Sub-Zero Blizzard Winds Scream Across Volcanic Peaks
beats.text: An intense 973 hPa North Pacific cyclone is wrapping violent 40.9 m/s (147 km/h) wind gusts into the rugged coast of Kamchatka at -11 °C, generating treacherous coastal seas and whiteout conditions across the peninsula.

beats.title: Sharpened by the Siberian Temperature Contrast
beats.text: Over the past two weeks, four separate gale events and more than six times the usual precipitation have struck eastern Kamchatka, energised by the sharp clash between bitter continental air and relatively mild Pacific waters.

beats.title: Top of the Late-November Gust Record
beats.text: Normal late-November peak gusts in this sector sit near 13 m/s; at over 40 m/s, this storm's wind core stands at the very top (#1 in 87 years, 99.4th percentile) of ERA5 late-November snapshots since 1940.

beats.title: Stronger Moisture Fuel for Subpolar Storms
beats.text: Regional late-autumn temperatures around the northwest Pacific rim have warmed by +0.9 °C since 1940-1979, supplying extra latent heat from condensation that can help explosive mid-latitude cyclones tighten their inner wind cores.

stories.kicker: THANKSGIVING COASTAL STORM · EASTERN UNITED STATES
stories.headline: Subtropical plume dumps 139 mm of rain along the US Atlantic seaboard
stories.region: North Carolina Outer Banks and Mid-Atlantic Coast

beats.title: Holiday Travel Meets a Turbocharged Coastal Low
beats.text: Just as millions travel for Thanksgiving, a deepening 1001 hPa coastal low off Cape Hatteras is sweeping 139 mm of heavy rain and 25 m/s (90 km/h) gusts up the Mid-Atlantic seaboard, raising coastal surge and localized flooding risks.

beats.title: Rapid Shift After a Dry Fortnight
beats.text: Unlike a multi-week stall, this system marks an abrupt pattern flip: only 21 mm of rain fell here across the preceding two weeks before a surge of +7.3 °C warmer-than-normal Gulf Stream air collided with an advancing trough.

beats.title: Unusual Tropical-Like Rainfall Rates for November
beats.text: Delivering nearly three weeks' worth of typical late-autumn rain in a single day, the offshore rainband's synoptic intensity ranks at the 99th percentile (#1 in 87 years) of late-November ERA5 dates back to 1940.

beats.title: Rapidly Warming Gulf Stream Waters
beats.text: In local ERA5 records, late-November air over the western Atlantic Gulf Stream boundary has warmed by a remarkable +3.0 °C since 1940-1979, doubling 90th-percentile heavy-rain occurrences from 3 to 6 per 40-year period.

stories.kicker: NORTH ATLANTIC STORM TRACK · ICELAND TO NORTHWEST EUROPE
stories.headline: Deep 975 hPa North Atlantic storm drives 133 km/h gales into southern Iceland
stories.region: Southern Iceland and the North Atlantic

beats.title: Subtropical Warm Conveyor Slams Into High Latitudes
beats.text: A vigorous 975 hPa North Atlantic depression is lashing southern Iceland's coast and ice caps with 36.9 m/s (133 km/h) gusts alongside 28 mm of mild, wind-driven rain at +6.5 °C, while sending brisk frontal bands towards Ireland and Scotland.

beats.title: A Relentless Conveyor of Autumn Storms
beats.text: An energetic North Atlantic jet stream has aimed storm after storm along this corridor: southern Iceland has recorded 9 gale days over the past two weeks and 229 mm of precipitation across the last 28 days.

beats.title: More Than Double Normal Late-November Gusts
beats.text: Peak gusts near 37 m/s are more than twice the 1991-2020 seasonal average of 16.8 m/s for this date, placing today's landfalling wind core in the top 1% of late-November storms in the 1940-2026 ERA5 record.

beats.title: Rain Replacing Snow on Subarctic Glaciers
beats.text: Southern Iceland has warmed by +1.6 °C in late November since 1940-1979, and today's storm carries a +4.5 °C warm anomaly, meaning moisture that historically fell as early-winter snow increasingly falls as heavy rain onto coastal glaciers.
